result.summary: Allows running -txindex concurrently with block pruning as long as the index contains no legacy file-offset entries. When a transaction lookup targets a block that has been pruned from disk, txindex lookups return candidate block hashes so RPC and REST callers can distinguish missing transactions from pruned ones. Callers can then retrieve missing blocks on demand with getblockfrompeer and retry.
result.problem: -txindex and -prune have historically been mutually exclusive because legacy txindex entries referenced direct file positions on disk. Users running storage-constrained pruned nodes could not maintain a transaction index to track or look up confirmed transactions.
evidence: Resolves multiple long-standing issues requesting txindex support on pruned nodes: #10609, #12651, #16182, and #35240.
result.scope_notes: Changes RPC error structures: JSONRPCError now supports an optional error.data object, which getrawtransaction and gettxoutproof use to supply candidate pruned_block_hashes.
result.changed_since_previous: Removed the partial indexing feature that allowed initializing txindex from the oldest retained block and exposing start height in getindexinfo; nodes must still index blocks before they are pruned.
result.card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning when the index contains no legacy file-offset entries. When a transaction lookup targets a pruned block, GetTransaction, REST, and RPC calls (getrawtransaction, gettxoutproof) surface candidate block hashes in error data so callers can fetch the block via getblockfrompeer and retry. It addresses several issues opened since 2017 requesting txindex support on pruned nodes (#10609, #12651, #16182, #35240).

risk.why: Mistakes in candidate block reporting or txindex lookup logic could cause incorrect RPC error data or crashes during pruned block queries.
